title: Annotatio III §.IV: Sixth century — sacred image use and cult arise in temples; once unheard-of and hated
pass_a_gloss: For it happened that when the Apostolic, truly Episcopal and Patristic centuries of the Catholic Church were finished — or at least with the end of them all imminent — about the sixth century the use and cult of sacred images began to grow strong in temples, in earlier times not only utterly unheard-of, but even from the public Confession of all Protestants hated in a greater degree.
pass_b_english: When the Apostolic / Episcopal / Patristic centuries were spent (or nearly ended), about the sixth century sacred-image use and cult began to strengthen in temples.
Earlier ages had never heard of it; Protestant public Confessions hate it still more.
source_text: Enimvero accidit, ut exactis Seculis Ecclesiæ Catholicæ Apostolicis, verè Episcopalibus atque Patristicis, saltem fine hisce cunctis imminente, Seculo admodum sexto imaginum sacrarum usus cultusque in templis invalescere inciperet, superioribus temporibus non tantùm inauditus prorsus, sed etiam ex omnium Protestantium Confess. publica majorem in modum exosus.
